title: Marco Polo Bridge incident
summary: On 7 July 1937, during Japanese army exercises near the Marco Polo Bridge southwest of Beiping, Japanese troops asked to enter Wanping to look for a missing soldier. The Chinese side refused and fighting began. After this clash, Japan and China remained at war continuously until 1945.

uncertainty.note: Clash begins on the night of 7 July 1937; later fighting not dated here.

where.modern_name: Marco Polo Bridge (Lugouqiao) and Wanping, southwest of central Beijing, China (pin is the Wanping Fortress, a proxy for the bridge area)
where.historical_name: Marco Polo Bridge (Lugouqiao) and Wanping, near Beiping, Republic of China

importance.justification: Clash widely treated as the start of the continuous Sino-Japanese war of 1937-1945.

sources.title: The Marco Polo Bridge Incident and the Outbreak of the Total War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression
sources.publisher: Chinese Culture Promotion Office, Hong Kong SAR Government

sources.title: GPS coordinates of Wanping Fortress, China

reviewer_note: Coordinates are a rounded Wanping Fortress pin from a secondary aggregator, not a surveyed bridge point; verify. Sources describe the fighting only briefly; Government source has a Chinese-perspective framing.
